clue.text: One working with Ruby possibly about to speak

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Someone who works alongside a woman called Ruby is on the point of saying something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby looks like a colleague's name, capitalised to mislead; it is the gemstone, and 'possibly' marks it as one example of a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem cutter shapes and faces precious stones, rubies among them.

clue.text: Asian feature ends in the cretaceous age

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: the final letters of the next three words are taken, the ends found in each

explanation.surface: A characteristic trait of Asia, seen in the rocks of the Cretaceous period.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from China is Asian; the answer is a particular kind of Asian.

clue.text: Darts, then dancing in London street (familiar to many here)

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set dancing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Throwing darts and then going dancing out on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar to many here' nods to the Strand being a square on the London Monopoly board, which many solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a famous thoroughfare in central London running from Trafalgar Square towards the City.

clue.text: Annabel ate dripping sandwiches in high spirits

indicators.note: the three words hold the answer between their outer parts, as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: Annabel ate sandwiches with dripping on them and was in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' reads as food Annabel ate; it is the signal that the words contain the answer: annabEL ATE Dripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Being elated means feeling joyful and buoyant, the same as being in high spirits.

clue.text: Having difficulty caring about EU backing massacre

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the other piece
letters having difficulty are in trouble and jumbled out of order
EU backing means those two letters read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to care about the European Union's support for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having difficulty' is the anagram signal and 'backing' the reversal one, though both read as plain description; 'about' puts the jumbled letters round the turned pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The bombing of the Basque town in 1937, painted by Picasso, is remembered as a massacre of civilians.

clue.text: State you visit in the end, I understand

parts.note: U is text shorthand for you

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word visit is used

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of comprehension, as in 'ah, I see'

explanation.surface: A US state you get to visit eventually, as far as I can tell.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty United States, in the west, with Salt Lake City as capital.

clue.text: Indecency has French author requiring bodyguards

parts.note: Jean Racine was a 17th-century French dramatist
the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard unit, the Schutzstaffel

explanation.surface: A tale of indecency involving a French writer who needs protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness is the quality of being suggestive or risqué, close to indecency.

clue.text: Language guess (not first time)

indicators.note: the first time letter only is dropped, leaving the later one

parts.note: to intuit is to know by instinct, to guess

explanation.surface: A language guessing game, now on its second go.
explanation.walkthrough: INTUIT has two Ts; 'not first' removes only the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic peoples of Canada and Greenland speak a tongue known by their own name.

clue.text: Answer, beginning with European goddess

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: The solution, it turns out, starts with a goddess from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Phoenician and Canaanite deity of fertility and love, known as Ashtoreth in the Bible.

clue.text: Simple scratch oddly missing — it makes you sick

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are missing, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A simple scratch, with something strange about it, that makes you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of SIMPLE and SCRATCH leaves I P E and C A C. 'Simple' also means a medicinal herb, which fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a root extract used as an emetic, a drug given to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Where to hear a criminal crawl out

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain crawls out of a hiding place, somewhere listeners might catch him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the legal sense: a court hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears cases in a tribunal room, so this is where trials are heard.

clue.text: Doctor against stopping genuine purge

indicators.note: the doctor and against pieces are stopping up, plugging, the inside of the other word

parts.note: real means genuine
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A doctor objecting to a genuine purge of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is a clearing out, getting rid of unwanted people or things.

clue.text: Highly-valued French art packed the place

parts.note: in French tu es means thou art, so es is art
crowds that teemed filled every corner

explanation.surface: Prized French art drew such crowds the gallery was packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something esteemed is held in high regard and greatly respected.

clue.text: Most of train returns for one joining

indicators.note: the shortened word returns, reading backwards
most of the word means its final letter is lost

parts.note: a train of attendants is a retinue

explanation.surface: Most of a train comes back for a single passenger to get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a group of followers, not a railway train; RETINU reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that unites brings things together, so it is one that joins.

clue.text: Home Guard end up surrounding illuminated island

indicators.note: the reversed word is put surrounding the other pieces
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal
lit means illuminated

explanation.surface: The Home Guard finish by circling an island lit up at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the goal word round to MIA, which 'surrounding' wraps about the other pieces. The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer reserve in World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: A home guard is a citizen army of non-professional soldiers raised for local defence.

clue.text: Dairy product manufactured backwards

indicators.note: the word is read backwards, from its last letter

parts.note: manufactured means made

explanation.surface: A dairy product produced in the reverse order from usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coat, and cheese is a dairy product.

clue.text: 18th-century style appropriate after Lesotho accepts French agreement

indicators.note: the word for appropriate comes after the other piece
the country code accepts, takes in, the French word

parts.note: LS is the international code for Lesotho
oui is French for yes
to appropriate is to seize

explanation.surface: A neat style of furniture adopted when Lesotho signs a deal with France.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative style of the reign of Louis XVI, a late 18th-century fashion in furniture and design.

clue.text: As part of game, the French leave stones on the beach, causing invasion

parts.note: in means as part of
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the French word leaves, is removed from, the beach stones

parts.note: shingle is beach pebbles
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Part of a game in which French players walk off the pebbly beach and an invasion follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flooding in, like an invading army pouring in.

clue.text: Dog keeping new queen calm

indicators.note: the dog word keeps, holds within it, the other pieces

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them

explanation.surface: A dog guarding a recently crowned queen stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb meaning follow, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil describes a peaceful, untroubled state, the same as calm.

clue.text: Nearly all German, the staff in charge of civic dignitaries

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, with its last letter lost

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
der is German for the
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Almost every German employee in charge of the town's dignitaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermen are senior members of a borough council, so the adjective relates to such civic office-holders.

clue.text: Prince of Israel's able-bodied dancer loses footing

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the last letter, and it is lost

parts.note: Salome danced before Herod for John the Baptist's head

explanation.surface: A fit Israeli dancer slips and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Israel's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was the rebellious son of King David in the Bible, a prince of Israel.

clue.text: Sailor holding artist's horse

indicators.note: the sailor holds the artist within

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A sailor holding an artist's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian is a famous breed of horse from the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: On the banks of Russian river, going up with 1D?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a town by a river stands on its banks
the Ob is a great river of Siberia
and means with

explanation.surface: Something on the banks of a Russian river, going upstream with a cross-referenced entry.
explanation.walkthrough: '1D' looks like a cross-reference to 1 Down but means One Direction, the pop group; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: One Direction was a famous group of young male pop singers, an example of the genre.

clue.text: European port has primitive support for life

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is below, supporting the first

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original

explanation.surface: A port in Europe offers basic life support.
explanation.definitionFit: Life in the sense of liveliness and energy, as in 'full of life', is vigour.

clue.text: Inscrutable character cross after quietly breaking lower leg

indicators.note: the cross comes after the other piece
the soft letter breaks into the leg word

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
P is piano, quietly in music
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A poker-faced person, crossed after quietly breaking his shin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sphinx, with its riddles and impassive stone face, is a byword for an enigmatic person.

clue.text: Monopolise almost any hut

parts.note: to hog is to keep all to yourself

indicators.note: almost all of the word, its final letter cut

explanation.surface: Taking over almost any hut for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Navajo dwelling of earth and timber, a kind of hut.

clue.text: Dancer I get into New Jersey, apparently flying

indicators.note: I goes into the state abbreviation

parts.note: NJ is the US state abbreviation
something in the sky is apparently flying

explanation.surface: A dancer arriving in New Jersey seems to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' marks IN SKY as a loose, playful equivalent of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was the celebrated Russian ballet dancer famous for his leaps.

clue.text: Trees which have teeth

definitions.meaning: eucalyptus and other trees that exude resin
the flesh in the mouth that holds the teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees are eucalypts; the gums of the mouth have teeth set in them.

clue.text: Famous can-can dancer's delay over extremely unusual utterance

parts.note: a lag is a delay
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the extremes, first and last letters, of each of the two words

explanation.surface: The famous can-can dancer's hesitation over a very odd remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'dancer's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise Weber, painted by Toulouse-Lautrec, was the star of the Moulin Rouge can-can under the stage name 'The Glutton'.

clue.text: Look drunk getting a book

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Seeming drunk after picking up a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's controversial 1955 novel is a celebrated book.

clue.text: Picture animals needing oxygen supply

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A picture of animals that need an oxygen supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as a noun but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Cold following stiff

parts.note: F is short for following, as in page references
rigid means stiff

explanation.surface: Cold after being stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means intensely cold, as in a frigid winter or a chilly manner.
